stance.label: Short-term bearish · long-term valuation in the bottom zone

headline: 62K broke on a close: the thickest short-term holder layer failed, coins are thin down to the prior low near 58.5K, and this leg is not done.
summary: Short-term bearish: the close broke 62K, ETFs lost another $310M on Nov 18, US stocks keep falling and more accounts hold longs, not fewer. Long-term bullish: only 45% of supply is in profit and unrealized profit relative to market cap matches the 2022 bottom's lowest reading, a bottom-zone valuation. A close below 60.5K takes long-term holder losses to a cycle high, with the prior low at 58.5K next; a floor needs ETF flows to turn net positive first.

watch.label: 200-day MA
watch.note: 8 straight closes below; a close back above needs +17.3%

overview.lead: The 62K that held intraday yesterday did not hold at today's close: 61,914 is a new low for the leg from Sep 21.
points: Intraday range 61,353–64,014; the morning bounce was fully given back and the close sits in the bottom fifth of the range, on volume 1.3x the 20-day average.
US equities fell across the board the same day, a sixth straight loss for the S&P 500; Fear & Greed is 10, a seventh day of extreme fear.
November to date is −20.1%; the worst November since 2013 was 2018 at −37.0%.
The framework did nothing new today; the market-stage label is unchanged, but one of its premises loosened (see the cycle page).

cycle.lead: Long-term valuation is a notch cheaper while the trend lost a pillar: the 200-day MA is now below where it stood 30 days ago.
points: This page's finding: the market stage is still bull, day 42, but the 200-day MA at 72,637 has turned down and all 6 supporting lights are now off.
Relative unrealized profit is 33.6%, a sixth day under the floor and equal to the lowest reading of the 2022 bottom stretch (Bitview, Nov 19).
The Dawn Index heat is 5.6, in the Night stage; the weekly bull/bear score is −1.2, from +0.32 last week. One measures valuation and the other trend, and they point opposite ways.
The validation window for the Jun 30 low at 58,525 runs to Dec 19 and the close is 5.5% above it; the Tidemark bottom signal is 38.1, still short of 50.

market.lead: The leg from Sep 21 is down 28.5%, already deeper than the deepest pullback of the last bull market.
points: The deepest pullback of the previous cycle (2022–2025) was −28.2% in April 2025; this leg has run 59 days and sits 15.0% below its end line at 71,201.
The one-year position is the 3.6th percentile: lower than 96% of closes in the past year.
The Sell Pressure Index is at 100 for a tenth day with momentum at 0.08, so the bottom combo still stands; in 20 cases since 2012 price was higher 30 days later 11 times, about the same as any day.

deriv.lead: Price made a new low and more accounts are long, not fewer: 78.3% on Binance, in the top 1% of readings since 2021.
points: Longs are being flushed and longs are stepping in: $958M of longs were liquidated in 7 days, 81.6% of all liquidations (Coinalyze).
Open interest is down 4.8% in 7 days, so leverage has begun to come off, yet it is still up 5.4% over 30 days against a 25.3% price drop; weighted funding is 3.22% and OKX has turned negative.
Options keep buying protection: 7-day implied vol is 3.7 points above 90-day, the 25-delta risk reversal is −7.77, and premium flow has favored puts for 22 days.

The estimated long-liquidation band is 59.8–61.3K (2.3% below the close; several exchanges, an estimate), and dealers' largest estimated negative gamma sits at 60,000, so a move toward it would amplify volatility. The book shows $107M of bids at 60,000, on Hyperliquid perps.

flows.lead: Money is still leaving, and faster: ETFs lost $307M on Nov 18 and the 20-trading-day sum is −$3.695B.
points: This ETF outflow stretch is closing in on February's trough of −$3.885B; the June stretch reached −$5.64B (CoinMarketCap).
Coinbase spot takers sold a net 9,378 BTC in 7 days, the lowest position since the data began in August 2021; the three spot venues together sold a net 12,366 BTC (Coinalyze).
Stablecoins stand at $285.2B, down $16.4B in 30 days; realized cap is −0.71% over 30 days, a sixth day below zero (DefiLlama; CoinMetrics Nov 18).
The Korea premium is 2.43%, so Asia still pays up; USDT trades at 0.9988 to the dollar as stablecoins keep being redeemed for dollars.

onchain.lead: Sellers are more crowded than yesterday, and the only visible buyers are the very largest addresses.
points: This page's finding: the close fell beneath the thickest short-term holder band at 62–64K, and all 780K BTC in it are now underwater (Bitview, Nov 19).

96.3% of short-term holder coins are underwater; they realized 11,950 BTC of losses against 1,792 BTC of profit on the day. Concentrated loss-taking is in its tenth day, with intensity easing from 3.65 to 3.35.
Long-term holders realized $3.02B of losses over 7 days, from $2.74B yesterday; their loss share is 44.6%, less than 1 point from this cycle's 45.4% peak.
By address balance tier, addresses with 10K+ BTC added 45K BTC in 7 days while the 1K–10K tier shed 34K; breakeven for a 20 J/TH rig at $0.06 power is 63,102, now above the close.

exit.lead: Nothing new under the framework today: the hedge buy-back was already met on Nov 17, and the MVRV Z 7-day average slipped to 0.40 (CoinMetrics, Nov 18).

MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak is 0.424, far from the 0.75 line (111,338); the three top indicators read 9 / 8 / 37, all low.

news.title: S&P 500 fell 2.0% to 7,177, a sixth straight loss and the longest streak since April 2024; the Dow lost more than 1,100 points, the Nasdaq 2.23%, and all 11 sectors closed lower
news.read: On the day the US selloff broadened beyond tech, BTC closed below 62K. Over two months BTC is down 23.8% against 9.9% for the Nasdaq (to Nov 18): it fell first and further. Until equities stop falling, 60.5K and the prior low at 58.5K stay in play. No change to the cycle read.

news.title: BTC fell to about 61,800 intraday, its lowest since early July, and is heading for a seventh weekly loss; the 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.11% and the Philly Fed index dropped from 20.9 to 6.3 while prices paid rose to 58.2

Our 2-year yield sits 0.76 points above the policy ceiling, with no sign of looser money. Seven weekly losses describes price; what we track is who sells, and short-term holders have sold at a loss for 14 days.

news.title: Fed Governor Waller backs a 50 bp hike in December and futures price 25 bp in both December and January; meanwhile wholesale gasoline is down about 20% in three weeks and the AAA national average is $3.75, down 12.8% in a month
news.read: The hikes are almost fully priced, and falling fuel is the case for a softer CPI on Dec 10. What matters for BTC is whether the direction turns: the 2-year yield has to come down first, and our reading is 4.76%, still above the policy ceiling. There is no answer on this before the Dec 9 FOMC.

findings.title: Below a broken 62K the coins are thin and sellers are in more of a hurry than buyers
findings.lean_why: The thickest short-term holder layer has flipped underwater, coins are thin from here to the prior low, and the flow data shows no buyer taking the other side.
findings.what: 62K did not hold, and there is little beneath it to absorb selling: the close at 61,914 sits under the thickest short-term holder band at 62–64K (Bitview, Nov 19).
findings.why: The question is who sells below 62K and who buys. Start with sellers. Short-term holders are still the main force: 11,950 BTC of realized losses against 1,792 BTC of profit on the day, 96.3% of their coins underwater, and STH-SOPR below 1 for 14 straight days. Long-term holders are selling with them: $3.02B of realized losses in 7 days, from $2.74B yesterday, with the LTH-SOPR 7-day average at 0.86. Network-wide aSOPR (7-day average) is 0.962, the lowest since the data began in November 2023. Next, the cost map: the two thickest short-term holder bands are 62–64K with 780K BTC and 64–66K with 550K BTC, both now above the close, so support has become break-even supply; within 5% of the close the thinnest $1,000 band is 59K with only 83K BTC across all holders, against 690K BTC at 63K. Comparing two points in time: 550K BTC moved at a loss in the last 7 days, 470K of them landing in 62–64K; over 30 days short-term holders grew from 3.66M to 3.84M BTC and long-term holders shrank from 16.44M to 16.27M BTC (Bitview, actual coin age), and coins with a cost above 88K, a zone price never touched, fell by 140K BTC, which can only be selling at a loss. Of coins bought in these 30 days and not yet moved, an estimated 380K BTC sit in the 64K band (an estimate; the model is 2.6% off the actual short-term holder total). The buy side shows three things: by address balance tier, addresses with 10K+ BTC added 45K BTC in 7 days; the order book has $107M of bids at 60,000; and OKX spot takers bought a net 199 BTC on the day. Money says the opposite: ETFs lost $307M on Nov 18, Coinbase spot takers sold a net 9,378 BTC in 7 days, and stablecoins are down $16.4B in 30 days.
findings.alt: The other path is a false break: the close is less than $100 under 62,000, and if the book and the large addresses absorb the selling, a close back above 64K within a day or two would void this finding. Data limits: Bitview is per-UTXO with no entity clustering, so exchange wallet housekeeping counts as coins moved at a loss; address tiers are not entities, and growth in the largest tier may be exchange or custody wallets; order-book bids are a snapshot and can be pulled. Part of the long-term holder loss selling is coins bought high in May–June that only just passed 155 days.
findings.history: Lower price with heavier loss-taking has mostly appeared late in a decline, but often not for the last time: in 58 cases since 2013, price was higher 30 days later 44 times, with a median of +6.9% (any day: +2.8%). In the last three bear markets the largest long-term holder losses came at the bottom; this cycle's largest so far is 0.292% of market cap on Jun 30, against 0.242% now, so it has not been exceeded. The first loss floor has been broken only 6 times since 2012, and April 2014 and November 2018 were followed by further drops of 52% and 34%.
findings.so: What changed is the role of the 62–66K layer: yesterday it was support, today 1.33M short-term holder BTC sit above the close. What did not change is the long-term valuation read. The downside scenario: at a close of 60,000, 98.5% of short-term holders would be underwater, and that is also where the estimated long-liquidation band (59.8–61.3K) and dealers' largest estimated negative gamma sit, three things stacked on one price; at an estimated 60,500 the long-term holder loss share passes this cycle's 45.4% peak, which means the June bottom gets tested again. A (the thickest layer failed) has happened, so a bounce meets break-even supply first; B (long-term holder losses at a new high) has not, so June as the cycle low still stands.
findings.next: By Nov 26: a long-term holder loss share above 45.4% (a close below roughly 60,500) means the pain of this cycle exceeds June and the next level is the prior low at 58,525. A close back above 64,000 in the same window means today was a false break and the 780K BTC at 62–64K become support again.

findings.title: The 200-day MA has turned down and the bull label's premise is loosening
findings.lean_why: Every trend-side support has weakened and the 200-day MA has gone from rising to falling; long-term valuation is still cheap, but nothing on the trend side backs the bull label any more.
findings.what: The site's bull-market label lost a pillar today: the 200-day MA at 72,637 is now below its level of 30 days ago, 72,649 (Kraken closes, Nov 19).
findings.why: This comes from the hard-coded market-stage rule, not from a triggered signal. Bull is defined as 30 straight closes above a rising 200-day MA; the close has now been below the line for 8 days and the line itself turned down today, day 1. Under the rule it takes 30 straight closes below a falling MA to leave the bull stage, Dec 18 at the earliest. Taking the trend apart, no piece is still standing: all 6 supporting lights are off, the last of them, exchange supply, going out today; the weekly bull/bear score is −1.2, from +0.32 last week; the 50-week MA at 74,419 is 20.2% above the close. Price itself is outside the range of a bull-market pullback: down 28.5% from Sep 21, against −28.2% for the deepest one of the last bull. On the other side is valuation: Dawn Index heat at 5.6, in the Night stage, and relative unrealized profit at 33.6% (Bitview). The two do not conflict; one speaks to cheapness and the other to direction.
findings.alt: The 200-day MA is only $12 below its level of 30 days ago, which is flat; if price reclaims the line quickly the slope turns back up and the stage continues. The limit lies in the rule: it uses only closes and the moving average and reacts slowly; price was above 80K when the stage turned bull on Oct 9, and the label has not changed with price more than 20% lower. CryptoQuant, using a 365-day MA definition, has called it a bear market since Nov 17.
findings.history: After a close below the 50-week MA, price has often stayed under it for most of a year: the last two breaks, April 2022 and November 2025, lasted 49 and 44 weeks, and this one happened on Nov 8. The Dawn Index Night stage (valuation in the bottom zone) covers 62 past weeks; one year later price was higher every time and six months later 74% of the time, with nothing in that statistic about the path in between.
findings.so: What changed is how much weight "bull market, day 42" can bear: it will stay on the front page, but from today it is on a countdown. What did not change is the exit framework, which ignores the market stage; the price ladder and the MVRV lines are still far away. Yesterday we wrote that if the 200-day MA flattened further the premise of this stage would be tested; the test has begun.
findings.next: By Nov 25: 6 straight closes below a falling 200-day MA would mean the turn is not a one- or two-day blip and the 30-day count toward leaving the bull stage keeps running. A close back above this leg's end line at 71,201 by Nov 26 would mean the down leg is over and the MA has a chance to flatten again.

items.title: Wall Street Bought at $80,000. What Now?
items.points: ETFs took in a net $6.36B in the third quarter at a flow-weighted entry near 78,300; the fourth quarter to Nov 17 has seen $3.09B leave, 49% of that inflow. The base case this week is 61,800–69,400, leaning toward a retest of 62,029 and the 61,300 lower edge of the July base; acceptance below 61,300 with ETF outflows above $300M a day points to the Jul 1 low at 57,803. Three straight sessions of ETF inflows and STH-SOPR back at 1 would bring 69,400 and 72,700 into view.
items.meaning: Most of its bearish conditions were met today: ETFs lost $307M on Nov 18 and the intraday low at 61,353 sat right on its 61,300. Our estimated ETF holder cost is 21.6% above the close, the same direction as its figure; the definitions differ, so we do not subtract one from the other.

items.title: Book Churn: How Fast the Order Book Is Being Rewritten
items.points: A new metric, Book Churn: how often order-book price levels are revised per ten minutes, scored against the same hour over the prior 30 days. A score of 2+ is followed by an above-median-volatility hour 63.2% of the time (50% baseline), statistically level with a price-range signal at 63.7%; it has no direction.
items.meaning: A methodology piece with no BTC price view. Yesterday the book showed $233M of bids at 62,000 and today the close broke it, which is its point exactly: bids are a snapshot. The same goes for today's $107M at 60,000.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Capitulation Meets Support
items.points: BTC fell to 62K on Nov 15 with realized losses at levels first seen since early 2023; 62–66K holds about a fifth of short-term holder supply; the remaining long-liquidation band is 59.5–62.2K; reclaiming 74.1K would look like a base, while a daily close below 62K points to 58.5K and the realized price at 53.7K.
items.meaning: Its downside line, a daily close below 62K, was met today, and by its own account 58.5K is next. Our realized price is 53,418, close to its 53.7K; its long-liquidation band overlaps our estimated 59.8–61.3K.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 47
items.points: BTC fell about 13% on the week and briefly broke 63K; futures open interest was $34.2B, the lowest since August; 25-delta skew was 13.7%, the highest since August; ETFs lost $995M on the week; its conclusion was that leverage had been flushed and the market was less crowded.
items.meaning: We still disagree with "less crowded": 78.3% of Binance accounts hold longs, and open interest is up 5.4% in 30 days against a 25.3% price drop. The next Market Pulse is due Nov 22.
